creditorClaims.text: Claims must be filed in the probate office within 6 months after the grant of letters or 5 months after the first publication of notice, whichever is later; creditors entitled to actual notice have 30 days after notice; unfiled claims are forever barred (Ala. Code § 43-2-350).

earliestClose.text: No specific minimum is stated; distribution and final settlement follow the 6-month claims period of Ala. Code § 43-2-350, and executors must make annual settlements meanwhile (Ala. Code § 43-2-500).

smallEstate.text: Summary distribution without a personal representative by verified petition to the probate judge for a 'small estate' (personal property only, decedent owning no real property) whose value does not exceed the small estate amount, defined as the sum of the homestead allowance, exempt property and family allowance as adjusted every 3 years for inflation by the State Treasurer (Ala. Code §§ 43-2-691, 43-2-692, 43-8-116; Revised Alabama Small Estates Act, Act 2025-431).

simplified.text: Summary distribution of a small estate by petition to the judge of probate, with one published notice and notice to the Alabama Medicaid Agency (Ala. Code § 43-2-692, as revised by Act 2025-431).

filingFee.text: Judge of probate statutory fee of $45.00 for probate of a will (up to 5 pages, with 3 certified copies of letters and final settlement up to 10 pages) or grant of letters of administration (Ala. Code § 12-19-90(a)(1),(2)); counties may add other fees.

personalRepFee.text: Reasonable compensation fixed by the court considering listed factors, not exceeding 2.5% of the value of all property received and under the personal representative's control plus 2.5% of all disbursements; extra for extraordinary services (Ala. Code § 43-2-848).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule: the court fixes and allows the attorney's fee or compensation paid from the estate at each annual, partial or final settlement (Ala. Code § 43-2-682).

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 4 months after the first publication of notice to creditors, or within 3 years after death if notice was not published (AS 13.16.460(a)).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment, stating that notice to creditors was first published more than 6 months earlier (AS 13.16.630).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect property by affidavit if the entire estate, less liens and encumbrances, consists only of personal property not exceeding $50,000 plus registered vehicles with a total value not exceeding $100,000, and no personal representative application is pending (AS 13.16.680). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Summary administration: if the estate does not exceed family allowances, exempt property, administration costs, funeral and last-illness expenses, the personal representative may distribute and close at any time by verified statement (AS 13.16.690, 13.16.695).

filingFee.text: Superior court filing fee of $250.00 upon filing a trust or estate action other than registration or deposit of a will (Alaska Administrative Rule 9(b)(2)(A)).

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (AS 13.16.430), reviewable by the court (AS 13.16.440).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule: the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of any attorney employed by the personal representative (AS 13.16.440); reasonable attorney fees in good-faith estate litigation are paid from the estate (AS 13.16.435).

creditorClaims.text: The personal representative publishes notice once a week for 3 weeks; claims must be presented within 4 months after first publication, or for known creditors given written notice within the later of that period or 60 days after mailing (A.R.S. § 14-3801). Pre-death claims are in any event barred 2 years after death plus any remaining notice period (A.R.S. § 14-3803).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, a personal representative may close the estate by sworn closing statement no earlier than 4 months after the original appointment of a general personal representative, after determining that the claims period has expired (A.R.S. § 14-3933).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if no personal representative has been appointed and all personal property, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $200,000 (A.R.S. § 14-3971(B)); real property in Arizona up to $300,000 net of liens (assessed full cash value) can pass by affidavit of succession filed with the court no sooner than 6 months after death (A.R.S. § 14-3971(E)). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Informal probate and appointment before the registrar (A.R.S. Title 14, ch. 3, art. 3) and closing by sworn statement 4 months after appointment (A.R.S. § 14-3933); affidavit collection for personal property up to $200,000 and affidavit of succession for real property up to $300,000 (A.R.S. § 14-3971).

filingFee.text: Statutory clerk fee of $149.00 for an application for informal probate or appointment, or a petition in formal testacy or appointment proceedings (A.R.S. § 12-284(A), class C); statutory surcharges and local fees may be added by the clerk.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation (A.R.S. § 14-3719); the court may review its reasonableness on petition (A.R.S. § 14-3721).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule: the estate pays reasonable attorneys' fees (A.R.S. § 14-3720), which the court may review (A.R.S. § 14-3721); fiduciaries and their attorneys must manage costs prudently (A.R.S. § 14-1104).

creditorClaims.text: A creditor must file a claim before the later of 4 months after letters are first issued to a general personal representative or 60 days after notice of administration is mailed or delivered to the creditor (Prob. Code § 9100); this does not extend the 1-year limit of Code Civ. Proc. § 366.2.

earliestClose.text: No final distribution before the 4-month creditor claim period of Prob. Code § 9100 has run; the inventory and appraisal is due within 4 months after letters (Prob. Code § 8800).

smallEstate.text: Affidavit collection of personal property without probate if the gross value of the decedent's California real and personal property (excluding property described in § 13050, such as joint tenancy, trust and spousal property, and property in a § 13151 petition) does not exceed $208,850 for deaths on or after April 1, 2025 ($184,500 for deaths April 1, 2022 to March 31, 2025), and 40 days have elapsed since death (Prob. Code §§ 13100, 13101). The amount is adjusted every 3 years by the Judicial Council (Prob. Code § 890); next adjustment April 1, 2028 (form DE-300).

simplified.text: For deaths on or after April 1, 2025: court order determining succession to a primary residence worth up to $750,000 (Prob. Code § 13151); affidavit for real property of small value up to $69,625 (Prob. Code § 13200); small estate set-aside for spouse and minor children up to $107,900 net (Prob. Code §§ 6602, 6609); otherwise full probate, often with independent administration (Prob. Code § 10400 et seq.). Amounts from Judicial Council form DE-300 (rev. April 28, 2025).

filingFee.text: First-filed petition for letters of administration or letters testamentary: $435 (Gov. Code § 70650(a)), Statewide Civil Fee Schedule effective January 1, 2026, row 124; some counties add local surcharges (asterisk in schedule).

personalRepFee.text: Statutory compensation for ordinary services based on the estate accounted for (inventory value plus gains on sales plus receipts, less losses, without deducting encumbrances): 4% of the first $100,000, 3% of the next $100,000, 2% of the next $800,000, 1% of the next $9,000,000, 0.5% of the next $15,000,000, and a reasonable amount set by the court above $25,000,000 (Prob. Code § 10800).

attorneyFee.text: The attorney for the personal representative receives the same statutory percentages as the personal representative for ordinary services: 4% / 3% / 2% / 1% / 0.5%, court-set above $25,000,000 (Prob. Code § 10810).

creditorClaims.text: The published notice sets a claims date not earlier than 4 months after first publication (or 1 year after death if earlier) (C.R.S. 15-12-801); claims are barred after that date, after the date in a written notice, and in all cases 1 year after death (C.R.S. 15-12-803(1)).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment or 1 year after death, whichever occurs first (C.R.S. 15-12-1003(1)).

smallEstate.text: Ten days after death, successors may collect property by affidavit if the decedent's property subject to will or intestacy, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed twice the exempt-property amount of C.R.S. 15-11-403 as adjusted by C.R.S. 15-10-112 (C.R.S. 15-12-1201(1)(a)). The $30,000 exempt amount is increased by the CPI-U change since 2010, rounded down to $1,000: for deaths in 2026, 30,000 x (321.943 / 218.056 - 1) = 14,292.70, rounded down to 14,000, so $44,000 exempt property and an affidavit limit of $88,000 (computed).

simplified.text: Affidavit collection (C.R.S. 15-12-1201); summary administration when the estate does not exceed fiduciary property, allowances, administration, funeral and last-illness expenses (C.R.S. 15-12-1203); closing by sworn statement (C.R.S. 15-12-1003).

filingFee.text: Probate filing fees are set in C.R.S. Title 13 (not read).

personalRepFee.text: A fiduciary and its lawyer are entitled to reasonable compensation (C.R.S. 15-10-602(1)), judged under the factors of C.R.S. 15-10-603; the former UPC § 3-719 (C.R.S. 15-12-719) was repealed in 2011.

attorneyFee.text: The fiduciary's lawyer is entitled to reasonable compensation (C.R.S. 15-10-602(1)); no method of charging is presumed unreasonable (C.R.S. 15-10-603(2)).

creditorClaims.text: Connecticut has no general claims bar date: a fiduciary who pays or distributes in good faith is not chargeable for claims presented more than 150 days after appointment of the first fiduciary (C.G.S. § 45a-356); the fiduciary may give optional notice barring a claim not presented by a date at least 90 days after the notice (C.G.S. § 45a-357); all claims are limited to 2 years after death (C.G.S. § 45a-375(c)).

earliestClose.text: No statutory minimum; distribution is protected after the 150-day period following appointment of the first fiduciary (C.G.S. § 45a-356).

smallEstate.text: Small estate affidavit filed in the Probate Court instead of probate when the decedent's solely owned personal property (excluding property passing outside probate) does not exceed $40,000 and the decedent owned no solely owned Connecticut real property; the court issues a decree no earlier than 30 days after sending the affidavit to the Department of Administrative Services (C.G.S. § 45a-273). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Settlement of small estates by affidavit and Probate Court decree for personal property up to $40,000 with no solely owned real property (C.G.S. § 45a-273).

filingFee.text: For deaths on or after July 1, 2016 the Probate Court fee depends on the basis (greatest of inventory, succession/estate tax gross estate or Connecticut taxable estate; property passing to a surviving spouse counted at 50%): $25 up to $500; $50 up to $1,000; $50 + 1% of excess over $1,000 up to $10,000; $150 + 0.35% over $10,000 up to $500,000; $1,865 + 0.25% over $500,000 up to $2,000,000; $5,615 + 0.5% over $2,000,000 up to $8,877,000; $40,000 cap above; minimum $150 if a full estate is opened with a basis under $10,000 (C.G.S. § 45a-107(b)). The amount is value-based and is computed from the court-fee schedule in fees/connecticut.json (filingFee.amount left null to avoid double counting).

personalRepFee.text: No statutory percentage schedule for executors and administrators in the Connecticut General Statutes chapters read (chap. 802, 802b); compensation is reviewed by the Probate Court as reasonable.

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; attorney fees paid from the estate are reviewed by the Probate Court for reasonableness.

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 8 months of the decedent's death, whether or not notice to creditors was given (12 Del. C. § 2102(a)); post-death claims within 6 months after they arise (§ 2102(b)).

earliestClose.text: The executor or administrator has 1 year from the date of letters to settle the estate and is not required to distribute before then (12 Del. C. § 2311); legacies are payable 1 year from first appointment if no time is set (§ 2312).

smallEstate.text: Distribution without letters by affidavit 30 days after death if the personal estate (excluding jointly owned property and property in § 1901(b),(c)) does not exceed $50,000, debts are paid, the spouse's allowance is satisfied and the decedent owned no Delaware real estate (12 Del. C. § 2306). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Small estate affidavit filed with the Register of Wills for personal estates up to $50,000 with no Delaware real estate (12 Del. C. § 2306).

filingFee.text: Register of Wills fees are set by the governing body of each county and posted at each office (12 Del. C. §§ 2510, 2511); the New Castle County fee list was not read.

personalRepFee.text: Commissions are allowed as provided by rule of the Court of Chancery and may be reduced for late accounts (12 Del. C. § 2305); no percentage schedule in the statute.

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys' fees are allowed as provided by rule of the Court of Chancery (12 Del. C. § 2305); no statutory schedule.

creditorClaims.text: Claims are barred unless presented within 6 months after the date of first publication of notice of the appointment of a personal representative (D.C. Code § 20-903(a)(1)).

earliestClose.text: In unsupervised administration the personal representative closes the estate with a Certificate of Completion, which may not be filed before the time for filing creditors' claims has expired and after a 60-day objection period on the account sent to interested persons (D.C. Code § 20-735).

smallEstate.text: A small asset may be paid or delivered by affidavit of all known successors if the entire probate estate, less liens, does not exceed $40,000, includes no real property, and at least 60 days have passed since death (D.C. Code § 20-361; the online text includes temporary amendments expiring March 27, 2027).

simplified.text: Small estate administration in the Probate Division when the property subject to administration in D.C. is $80,000 or less (D.C. Code § 20-351, as amended by D.C. Law 25-302, effective March 21, 2025).

filingFee.text: Register of Wills fees are set by the Superior Court (D.C. Code § 15-707(a)); no fee for estates up to $500 and not more than $15 for estates up to $2,500 (§ 15-707(b)). The court's current fee schedule was not read.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (D.C. Code § 20-751), reviewable by the court using listed factors (D.C. Code § 20-753).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule: the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of an attorney employed by the personal representative, considering the work performed, estimates given, time spent and complexity (D.C. Code § 20-753).

sources.name: District of Columbia: closing the estate
District of Columbia: personal representative fees

creditorClaims.text: Claims are barred unless filed by the later of 3 months after the first publication of the notice to creditors or, for creditors who must be served, 30 days after service (Fla. Stat. § 733.702); all claims are barred 2 years after death whether or not letters issued (Fla. Stat. § 733.710).

earliestClose.text: The estate cannot be closed before the 3-month creditor period after first publication of the notice to creditors has run and timely claims are resolved (Fla. Stat. § 733.702); after administration is completed the personal representative is discharged (Fla. Stat. § 733.901).

smallEstate.text: Florida has no small-estate affidavit; the simplified route is summary administration, available if the estate subject to administration in Florida, less exempt property, does not exceed $150,000 (raised from $75,000 by ch. 2026-57, effective July 1, 2026) or the decedent has been dead more than 2 years, and the will does not direct formal administration (Fla. Stat. § 735.201). The amount is not indexed.

simplified.text: Summary administration for estates up to $150,000 net of exempt property or deaths more than 2 years ago (Fla. Stat. § 735.201); disposition without administration by court letter when the estate is only exempt property plus non-exempt personal property not exceeding preferred funeral expenses and last-60-days medical expenses (Fla. Stat. § 735.301).

filingFee.text: Clerk fee for formal administration: up to $395; summary administration $340 (estates of $1,000 or more) or $230 (under $1,000); disposition of personal property without administration $230; plus a $4 service charge on petitions for summary or formal administration (Fla. Stat. § 28.2401(1),(3)).

personalRepFee.text: Commission presumed reasonable in formal administration, on the inventory value of probate assets plus income earned during administration: 3% of the first $1 million, 2.5% from $1 million to $5 million, 2% from $5 million to $10 million, 1.5% above $10 million, plus reasonable compensation for extraordinary services (Fla. Stat. § 733.617).

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys receive reasonable compensation; a fee is presumed reasonable in formal administration if based on the compensable value: $1,500 up to $40,000, $2,250 up to $70,000, $3,000 up to $100,000, then 3% on the next $900,000, 2.5% from $1 million to $3 million, 2% from $3 million to $5 million, 1.5% from $5 million to $10 million, 1% above $10 million, plus extraordinary services; written disclosures are required to use the schedule (Fla. Stat. § 733.6171).

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented by the later of 4 months after first publication of notice to creditors or 60 days after written notice, or within 18 months after death if no notice was published or served (HRS § 560:3-803(a)).

earliestClose.text: Not verified: closing by sworn statement under HRS § 560:3-1003 was not read.

smallEstate.text: When a decedent leaves property in Hawaii worth no more than $100,000 and no personal representative has been appointed, the circuit court clerk may be authorized to administer the estate as personal representative (HRS § 560:3-1205, as amended by L 2000, c 48). The small-estate affidavit of HRS § 560:3-1201 could not be read.

simplified.text: Clerk administration of estates of $100,000 or less (HRS § 560:3-1205); collection by affidavit (HRS § 560:3-1201, not read).

filingFee.text: Probate filing fees not read.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services; no percentage schedule (HRS § 560:3-719).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney schedule in the sections read; attorney compensation is reviewable for reasonableness (HRS § 560:3-721, not read).

creditorClaims.text: A published notice requires claims within 4 months after first publication; creditors given written notice have the later of that period or 60 days after mailing (Idaho Code § 15-3-801); pre-death claims are barred at the earlier of 3 years after death or those periods (Idaho Code § 15-3-803).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment, after the claims period has expired (Idaho Code § 15-3-1003).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect property by affidavit if the fair market value of the probate estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 and no personal representative or summary administration is pending or granted (Idaho Code § 15-3-1201). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit collection up to $100,000 (Idaho Code § 15-3-1201); summary administration and informal probate under Idaho Code title 15, chapter 3.

filingFee.text: District court probate filing fees are set in Idaho Code title 31, chapter 32; the probate-specific amount was not located in § 31-3201 as read.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (Idaho Code § 15-3-719).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; attorney compensation is reviewable for reasonableness (Idaho Code § 15-3-721, UPC equivalent, not read).

creditorClaims.text: The representative publishes notice once a week for 3 weeks and mails it to known creditors; the claim date must be at least 6 months after first publication or 3 months after mailing, whichever is later (755 ILCS 5/18-3); claims not filed by that date are barred, and all claims are barred 2 years after death in any event (755 ILCS 5/18-12).

earliestClose.text: An independent representative may seek discharge by verified report stating that the 755 ILCS 5/18-3 notice was published and every claim is allowed, disallowed or barred (755 ILCS 5/28-11), so closing comes after the 6-month claims date.

smallEstate.text: Small estate affidavit (no court filing) when the gross value of the decedent's entire personal estate, including property passing by will or intestacy, does not exceed $100,000 (755 ILCS 5/25-1, as amended by P.A. 98-836, eff. January 1, 2015). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Small estate affidavit for personal estates up to $100,000 (755 ILCS 5/25-1); independent administration without court supervision, closed by verified report (755 ILCS 5/28-11).

filingFee.text: Probate filing fees are set by each circuit clerk under the Clerks of Courts Act; the Cook County Clerk of the Circuit Court probate fee schedule was not found on its website.

personalRepFee.text: A representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (755 ILCS 5/27-1).

attorneyFee.text: The attorney for a representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (755 ILCS 5/27-2(a)).

creditorClaims.text: Claims are barred unless filed with the clerk within the later of 4 months after the second publication of the notice to creditors or, for reasonably ascertainable creditors, 1 month after notice is mailed (Iowa Code § 633.410).

earliestClose.text: Final settlement must be made within 3 years after the second publication of the notice to creditors unless the court orders otherwise (Iowa Code § 633.473); no earlier date is fixed beyond the 4-month claims bar of § 633.410.

smallEstate.text: Distribution by affidavit 40 days after death when the gross value of the decedent's personal property passing by will or intestacy is $50,000 or less and there is no real property, and no administration is pending (Iowa Code § 633.356). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Administration of small estates under Iowa Code chapter 635 when gross probate assets in Iowa do not exceed $200,000: letters are issued by the clerk on petition (Iowa Code § 635.1).

filingFee.text: Clerk court costs equal to 0.2% of the value of the probate assets listed in the report and inventory (Iowa Code § 633.31(3)); non-probate assets such as joint tenancy property and beneficiary-designated accounts are excluded.

personalRepFee.text: Reasonable fees set by the court, not exceeding 6% of the first $1,000, 4% from $1,000 to $5,000 and 2% above $5,000 of the gross assets listed in the probate inventory (life insurance excluded unless payable to the estate) (Iowa Code § 633.197); extra allowances for extraordinary services (Iowa Code § 633.199).

attorneyFee.text: Reasonable fee set by the court, not exceeding the personal representative schedule of § 633.197 (Iowa Code § 633.198), plus extraordinary services (Iowa Code § 633.199).

creditorClaims.text: Demands are forever barred unless presented within the later of 4 months from first publication of notice to creditors or, for known or reasonably ascertainable creditors, 30 days after actual notice; creditors have no claim unless a probate or administration petition is filed within 6 months after death (K.S.A. 59-2239(1)).

earliestClose.text: No fixed minimum period read; the estate is closed by final settlement hearing and decree assigning the estate (K.S.A. 59-2249) after the 4-month claims period of K.S.A. 59-2239.

smallEstate.text: Personal property transferable to the estate may be delivered to a successor on affidavit, without letters, if the total probate assets do not exceed $75,000 (K.S.A. 59-1507b(a)). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Administration under the Kansas simplified estates act, with the court choosing simplified or supervised administration based on estate size, kinship, solvency and cost (K.S.A. 59-3202); Kansas informal administration act (K.S.A. 59-3301 et seq.).

filingFee.text: Probate docket fees are set by statute (K.S.A. 60-2001 and related sections); the amount was not read.

personalRepFee.text: Every fiduciary is allowed necessary expenses and compensation for services, and for its attorneys, that is just and reasonable; allowances may be requested during administration (K.S.A. 59-1717).

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys' compensation must be just and reasonable and is allowed by the court (K.S.A. 59-1717).

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 6 months after appointment of the personal representative, or within 2 years after death if no personal representative is appointed (KRS 396.011(1), effective June 29, 2021).

earliestClose.text: A personal representative may distribute the estate 6 months after qualification (KRS 395.190); an informal final settlement may be filed any time after 6 months from appointment (KRS 395.605(3)).

smallEstate.text: No affidavit procedure: the District Court may dispense with administration and transfer the assets when the surviving spouse's (or children's) $30,000 exemption under KRS 391.030, alone or with preferred claims paid by them, equals or exceeds the distributable assets (KRS 395.455, as amended effective July 15, 2026; KRS 391.030(1)(c)).

simplified.text: Order dispensing with administration (KRS 395.455); informal final settlement without hearing when the fiduciary is sole beneficiary or all beneficiaries sign verified waivers, after 6 months (KRS 395.605).

filingFee.text: Probate court costs are fixed by statute and Supreme Court rule; the amount was not read.

personalRepFee.text: Compensation of an executor or administrator may not exceed 5% of the value of the decedent's personal estate plus 5% of the income collected; the court may allow fair and reasonable extra compensation for extraordinary services, real estate or death-tax work on non-probate property (KRS 395.150).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney fee schedule; the attorney's fee must be disclosed in settlements (KRS 395.605(1)(e)) and is allowed by the court as reasonable.

creditorClaims.text: Louisiana has no general non-claim bar date for successions: creditors may present claims to the succession representative, and a formal sworn proof of claim suspends prescription for up to 10 years (La. C.C.P. art. 3245); payment of estate debts is authorized after a published notice with a 7-day opposition period (La. C.C.P. art. 3304).

earliestClose.text: No statutory minimum period; a petition to pay estate debts can be homologated 7 days after publication (La. C.C.P. art. 3304) and the representative's compensation is due on homologation of the final account (La. C.C.P. art. 3351).

smallEstate.text: A small succession is that of a Louisiana domiciliary leaving property with a gross value of $200,000 or less at death ($125,000 for ancillary successions of non-domiciliaries), or of any value if death occurred at least 20 years before the affidavit (La. C.C.P. art. 3421, last amended by Acts 2026, No. 293); it may be settled by small succession affidavit without judicial opening for intestate decedents and in the cases of art. 3431 (La. C.C.P. arts. 3431, 3432). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Small succession affidavit without court proceedings (La. C.C.P. arts. 3431-3432); heirs who accept may also be sent into possession without administration (not read).

filingFee.text: Succession filing costs are set by each parish clerk of court; the fee schedule was not read.

personalRepFee.text: Absent a provision in the testament or an agreement with the surviving spouse and heirs, the executor or administrator receives 2.5% of the amount of the inventory; the court may increase it if inadequate; due on homologation of the final account (La. C.C.P. art. 3351).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule for the succession attorney in the articles read; fees are reviewed by the court as reasonable.

creditorClaims.text: The published notice requires claims within 4 months after first publication (18-C M.R.S. § 3-801(1)); pre-death claims are barred at the earlier of 9 months after death or the notice periods of § 3-801 (18-C M.R.S. § 3-803(1)).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, the personal representative may close the estate by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment, after the claims period has expired (18-C M.R.S. § 3-1003(1)).

smallEstate.text: Collection by affidavit 30 days after death when the entire estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $40,000 adjusted for inflation (18-C M.R.S. § 3-1201(1)(A), as amended by PL 2025, c. 76). Under § 1-108 the $40,000 is increased by the change in the annual CPI-U from 2017 to the year before death, rounded down to $100: for deaths in 2026, 40,000 x (321.943 / 245.120 - 1) = 12,536.39, rounded down to 12,500, giving $52,500 (computed from the statute and BLS annual averages).

simplified.text: Summary administration when the estate does not exceed homestead allowance, exempt property, family allowance, administration costs, funeral and last-illness expenses (18-C M.R.S. § 3-1203); affidavit collection (§ 3-1201).

filingFee.text: Probate court filing fees were not read.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (18-C M.R.S. § 3-719), reviewable by the court (§ 3-721).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of any attorney employed by the personal representative (18-C M.R.S. § 3-721).

creditorClaims.text: Claims are forever barred unless presented by the earlier of 6 months after the decedent's death or 2 months after the personal representative mails or delivers a notice to the creditor (Md. Code, Est. & Trusts § 8-103(a)).

earliestClose.text: The first account is due within 9 months after appointment and further accounts every 6 months until the final account (Md. Code, Est. & Trusts § 7-305(a)); claims are barred 6 months after death (§ 8-103).

smallEstate.text: Small estate administration when the Maryland property subject to administration is worth $50,000 or less at death (fair market value less secured debts), or $100,000 or less when the surviving spouse is the sole legatee or heir (Md. Code, Est. & Trusts § 5-601). Not indexed. Maryland uses a simplified court procedure, not an out-of-court affidavit.

simplified.text: Small estate proceedings under Est. & Trusts §§ 5-602 to 5-607 for estates up to $50,000 ($100,000 if the spouse takes all) (§ 5-601).

filingFee.text: Register of Wills probate fee by value of the probate estate: under $50,000 $0; $50,000 to under $100,000 $100; to under $500,000 $200; to under $1,000,000 $1,000; to under $2,500,000 $2,000; to under $5,000,000 $5,000; to under $7,500,000 $7,500; to under $10,000,000 $10,000; $10,000,000 and over $10,000 plus 0.02% of the excess (Md. Code, Est. & Trusts § 2-206(b)(2)). The amount is value-based and is computed from the court-fee schedule in fees/maryland.json (filingFee.amount left null to avoid double counting).

personalRepFee.text: Reasonable compensation; commissions allowed by the court may not exceed 9% of property subject to administration up to $20,000, or $1,800 plus 3.6% of the excess over $20,000, unless the will provides more (Md. Code, Est. & Trusts § 7-601).

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys receive fair and reasonable compensation allowed by the court, and the court may not allow aggregate compensation (commissions plus counsel fees) above a fair and reasonable total charge for administering the estate (Md. Code, Est. & Trusts § 7-602).

creditorClaims.text: Not verified: M.G.L. c. 190B § 3-803 (limitations on presentation of claims) could not be read from an official source.

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment, after the time for presenting claims has expired (M.G.L. c. 190B § 3-1003(a)).

smallEstate.text: Voluntary administration by verified statement filed with the Probate and Family Court, 30 days after death, when the estate consists entirely of personal property not exceeding $25,000 in value plus a motor vehicle (M.G.L. c. 190B § 3-1201). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Voluntary administration for personal property up to $25,000 plus a car (§ 3-1201); summary administration when the estate does not exceed allowances, administration and funeral and last-illness expenses (M.G.L. c. 190B § 3-1203).

filingFee.text: Probate and Family Court: petition for formal or informal probate of a will and/or appointment of a personal representative $375 plus $15 surcharge; general probate petition $150 plus $15; subsequent letter $25.

personalRepFee.text: Not verified: M.G.L. c. 190B § 3-719 could not be read; no statutory percentage schedule is known from the sections read.

attorneyFee.text: Not verified: no statutory attorney fee schedule was found in the sections read.

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 4 months after publication of notice to creditors; known creditors have the later of 1 month after notice is sent or 4 months after publication; if notice requirements were not met, 3 years after death (MCL 700.3801, 700.3803(1)).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, the personal representative may close the estate by sworn closing statement no earlier than 5 months after original appointment, after the claims period has expired (MCL 700.3954).

smallEstate.text: Twenty-eight days after death, successors may collect property by sworn statement if the estate has no real property and its value, net of liens, does not exceed $50,000 adjusted annually for the cost of living (MCL 700.3983, as amended by 2024 PA 1, effective February 21, 2024); from January 1, 2024 the $50,000 is multiplied by the 2023 cost-of-living factor published by the Department of Treasury for the year of death and rounded to the nearest $1,000 (MCL 700.1210(2),(3)).

simplified.text: Court-ordered small estate assignment after payment of funeral and burial expenses when the remaining gross estate is $50,000 or less (as adjusted), filing fee $25 (MCL 700.3982, 600.880(2)); closing by sworn statement 5 months after appointment (MCL 700.3954).

filingFee.text: $150.00 filing fee to commence a probate proceeding (MCL 600.880(1)), plus an inventory fee on the date-of-death value of estate assets due before closing: e.g. $25 for $1,000 to under $3,000, $68.75 + 0.5% over $10,000 up to $25,000, $237.50 + 0.25% over $50,000 up to $100,000, $362.50 + 0.125% over $100,000 up to $500,000, then $62.50 per additional $100,000 (or larger fraction) above $500,000 and $31.25 per $100,000 above $1,000,000 (MCL 600.871).

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation and may pay it periodically as earned without prior court approval; attorneys serving as personal representative must keep time records (MCL 700.3719).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; attorney fees are a reasonable administration expense and must be disclosed in the closing account (MCL 700.3954(1)(d)).

creditorClaims.text: Creditors notified by publication must present claims within 4 months after the date of the court administrator's published notice; known creditors must be served within 3 months after first publication and have the later of 4 months after publication or 1 month after service (Minn. Stat. §§ 524.3-801, 524.3-803).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by statement no earlier than 4 months after original appointment, once notice to creditors was first published more than 4 months before (Minn. Stat. § 524.3-1003(a)).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit with a certified death record if the entire probate estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $75,000 (Minn. Stat. § 524.3-1201(a)). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Informal probate and closing by sworn statement 4 months after appointment (Minn. Stat. § 524.3-1003); collection by affidavit up to $75,000 (§ 524.3-1201).

filingFee.text: District court first-paper fee of $310 in every civil action or proceeding (Minn. Stat. § 357.021, subd. 2(1)); its application to probate petitions is assumed, not stated.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services, determined by the court considering listed factors (Minn. Stat. § 524.3-719).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of attorneys employed by the personal representative (Minn. Stat. § 524.3-721).

creditorClaims.text: Claims are barred unless filed within 6 months after the first published notice of letters, or 2 months after notice mailed or served on the creditor if later (RSMo § 473.360); all claims are barred 1 year after death whether or not administration is opened (RSMo § 473.444).

earliestClose.text: An independent personal representative may complete administration and be discharged after 6 months and 10 days from the first published notice of letters, by statement of account (RSMo § 473.840); supervised estates close by final settlement after 29 days' published notice (RSMo § 473.587).

smallEstate.text: Small estate affidavit 30 days after death when the entire estate, less liens, debts and encumbrances, does not exceed $40,000 and no letters are pending; a bond is required unless dispensed with, and the court fee and notice to creditors costs are paid (RSMo § 473.097, as amended by 2002 H.B. 1537). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Small estate affidavit procedure for estates up to $40,000 net (RSMo § 473.097); independent administration without court supervision with discharge by statement of account (RSMo § 473.840).

filingFee.text: Probate court costs are charged in amounts determined under RSMo §§ 488.010 to 488.020 (RSMo § 483.580); the dollar amounts are in the Missouri courts' court cost tables, not read.

personalRepFee.text: Minimum compensation of a sole personal representative on personal property administered and proceeds of real property sold under court order: 5% of the first $5,000, 4% of the next $20,000, 3% of the next $75,000, 2.75% of the next $300,000, 2.5% of the next $600,000, 2% above $1,000,000; the court allows more if reasonable (RSMo § 473.153(1)).

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys for the estate receive as a minimum the same percentages as the personal representative schedule, with additional reasonable compensation allowed by the court (RSMo § 473.153(3)).

creditorClaims.text: Published notice requires claims within 4 months after first publication; creditors given written notice have the later of that period or 30 days after mailing (MCA 72-3-801). Pre-death claims are barred at the latest 1 year after death (MCA 72-3-803).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, the personal representative may close the estate by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment, after the claims period has expired (MCA 72-3-1004).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if the probate estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 and no personal representative has been appointed (MCA 72-3-1101, last amended by Ch. 453, L. 2023). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Summary administration: if the estate, less liens, does not exceed the family allowances, exempt property, administration costs, funeral and last-illness expenses, the personal representative may distribute immediately without notice to creditors and file a closing statement (MCA 72-3-1103).

filingFee.text: Clerk of district court fee of $70 on filing an application for informal, formal or supervised probate or for appointment of a personal representative, including filing the will (MCA 25-1-201(1)(m)).

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (MCA 72-3-631, as amended by Ch. 313, L. 2019, which removed the former percentage cap); the court sets fees in a dispute (MCA 72-3-634).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule (former MCA 72-3-633 repealed by Ch. 313, L. 2019): the court reviews the reasonableness of compensation of any attorney employed by the personal representative and sets the fee in a dispute (MCA 72-3-634).

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 2 months after the first publication of notice to creditors (with a possible court extension of up to 30 days on application within 60 days), or within 3 years after death if notice was not given (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 30-2485(a)).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 5 months after original appointment, with notice to creditors first published more than 4 months earlier (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 30-24,117).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if all personal property in the estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 30-24,125). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Informal probate and closing by sworn statement after 5 months (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 30-24,117); affidavit collection of personal property up to $100,000 (§ 30-24,125).

filingFee.text: County court fee of $22 for probate proceedings commenced and closed informally (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 33-125(1)(a)(i)); other fees apply to formal proceedings and subsequent petitions.

personalRepFee.text: Compensation of the personal representative and of persons it employs is reviewable for reasonableness using listed factors such as time, skill, customary local fees and the amount involved (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 30-2482).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; attorney compensation is reviewed for reasonableness under the factors of Neb. Rev. Stat. § 30-2482.

creditorClaims.text: Claims must be filed with the clerk within 90 days after the first publication of notice to creditors (or after mailing, for creditors who must be mailed); mailed creditors have the later of 30 days after mailing or 90 days after publication; the period is 60 days in summary administration (NRS 147.040).

earliestClose.text: Not read: the final account follows the 90-day claims period (NRS 147.040); attorney compensation may be allowed after the creditor period (NRS 150.065).

smallEstate.text: Nevada small estate affidavit and set-aside procedures are in NRS chapter 146 and summary administration in NRS chapter 145; neither could be read.

simplified.text: Summary administration (NRS chapter 145) shortens the claims period to 60 days (NRS 147.040(4)); thresholds not read.

filingFee.text: County clerk fee of $72 on filing a petition for letters testamentary, letters of administration or setting aside an estate without administration when the stated estate value exceeds $2,500 (no fee at $2,500 or less) (NRS 19.013); additional court fees under NRS 19.0302 and local fees may apply (not read).

personalRepFee.text: Absent a will provision, fees on the whole estate accounted for, less liens and encumbrances: 4% of the first $15,000, 3% of the next $85,000, 2% above $100,000; the court may allow more if insufficient (NRS 150.020).

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys receive reasonable compensation based on hourly rate, estate value, agreement or a court-approved method; if based on estate value, the court allows 4% of the first $100,000, 3% of the next $100,000, 2% of the next $800,000, 1% of the next $9,000,000, 0.5% of the next $15,000,000 and a reasonable amount above $25,000,000, with a signed written agreement required (NRS 150.060).

creditorClaims.text: No action may be sustained against an administrator unless the demand was exhibited within 6 months after the original grant of administration (RSA 556:3), and no action may be begun within those first 6 months (RSA 556:1); suits on claims against the deceased must be brought within 1 year (RSA 556:5).

earliestClose.text: An administrator may move for summary administration to close the estate not less than 6 months after appointment, stating under oath that no debts or claims remain (RSA 553:33).

smallEstate.text: New Hampshire has no small-estate affidavit (the former voluntary administration statute, RSA 553:31, was repealed effective January 1, 2006); smaller estates get relief within administration, e.g. personal bond without sureties up to $25,000 gross and no publication of notice up to $10,000 gross (RSA ch. 553).

simplified.text: Waiver of administration (no inventory, bond or accounting) when the sole beneficiary or all beneficiaries/heirs serve as administrators (RSA 553:32); summary administration to close after 6 months (RSA 553:33).

filingFee.text: Circuit Court probate filing fees were not read.

personalRepFee.text: Not verified: no statutory percentage schedule was found in RSA chapters 553, 554 and 556 as read.

attorneyFee.text: Not verified: no statutory attorney fee schedule was found in the chapters read.

simplified.text: County Surrogates issue surviving-spouse and next-of-kin small estate affidavits (Essex County Surrogate: starting rate $65.00 each); statutory limits (N.J.S.A. 3B:10-3, 3B:10-4) not verified.

filingFee.text: Essex County Surrogate's Court: probate of a will of 2 pages or less $100.00, each additional page $5.00; first short certificate free, each additional $5.00; administration application $125.00. (Bergen, the most populous county, publishes no fee list on its website.)

personalRepFee.text: Not verified: New Jersey sets statutory corpus and income commissions (N.J.S.A. 3B:18-13, 3B:18-14), but the official statute text could not be read, so no schedule or fee file is given.

creditorClaims.text: Creditors should present claims within 7 months from the date letters are first issued to any fiduciary; a fiduciary who in good faith pays claims or distributes after that period is not liable for claims presented later (SCPA § 1802).

earliestClose.text: Distribution before the 7-month claims period of SCPA § 1802 runs is at the fiduciary's own risk, so estates are generally not closed before 7 months after letters issue (SCPA § 1802).

smallEstate.text: Voluntary administration (small estate) under SCPA Article 13 is available when the decedent's personal property has a gross value of $50,000 or less, excluding property set off to the family under EPTL 5-3.1(a) (SCPA § 1301); no waiting period after death is required (SCPA § 1304). The amount is not indexed.

simplified.text: Summary procedure by voluntary administrator (small estate affidavit filed with the Surrogate's Court) for personal property of $50,000 or less (SCPA §§ 1301, 1304); real property cannot pass through this procedure.

filingFee.text: Surrogate's Court fee on a petition for probate or letters depends on the gross estate: under $10,000 $45; $10,000 to under $20,000 $75; $20,000 to under $50,000 $215; $50,000 to under $100,000 $280; $100,000 to under $250,000 $420; $250,000 to under $500,000 $625; $500,000 and over $1,250 (SCPA § 2402(7)).

personalRepFee.text: Executor/administrator commissions on sums received and paid out: 5% of the first $100,000, 4% of the next $200,000, 3% of the next $700,000, 2.5% of the next $4,000,000, 2% above $5,000,000, computed half on receiving and half on paying out; specific legacies and devises are excluded from the base (SCPA § 2307).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule: the Surrogate's Court may fix and determine the compensation of the attorney for services rendered to the fiduciary (SCPA § 2110).

creditorClaims.text: The personal representative publishes notice once a week for 4 weeks naming a deadline at least 3 months after first publication (G.S. 28A-14-1(a)); claims not presented by that date, or within 90 days after notice is mailed or delivered to a known creditor if later, are forever barred (G.S. 28A-19-3(a)).

earliestClose.text: The final account is due within 1 year after qualifying (or 6 months after a State tax release, or at the annual account date, whichever is later) and may be filed voluntarily earlier with the clerk's approval (G.S. 28A-21-2(a),(a2)); it presupposes the 3-month creditor period of G.S. 28A-14-1.

smallEstate.text: Collection of personal property by affidavit filed with the clerk 30 days after death when personal property, less liens, does not exceed $20,000; up to $30,000 when the affiant is the surviving spouse and sole heir (intestate) or sole devisee (testate) (G.S. 28A-25-1, 28A-25-1.1). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Small estate affidavit procedure (G.S. 28A-25-1, 28A-25-1.1); payment of debts up to $5,000 owed to the decedent to the clerk of superior court (G.S. 28A-25-6); summary administration for a surviving spouse (G.S. Chapter 28A, Article 28).

filingFee.text: Costs in estate administration: $10.00 facilities fee, $4.00 technology fee and $106.00 General Court of Justice fee plus 40 cents per $100 of gross estate (personalty and sale proceeds of realty, not realty itself), the value-based part capped at $6,000, minimum $15.00 per filing (G.S. 7A-307(a)(1),(1a),(2)).

personalRepFee.text: Commissions fixed by the clerk of superior court, not exceeding 5% of receipts (including personal property when received) and of expenditures made according to law; no commission on distributions to heirs or devisees; realty sale proceeds count only when applied to debts or devises (G.S. 28A-23-3).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; the clerk may allow counsel fees to an attorney serving as personal representative for professional services beyond routine administration (G.S. 28A-23-4); fees of attorneys hired by the estate are paid as reasonable administration expenses approved by the clerk.

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 3 months after the first publication and mailing of notice to creditors, or within 3 years after death if notice was not published and mailed (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-19-03(1)).

earliestClose.text: A personal representative may close an unsupervised estate by verified statement, but not until 3 months after the first publication and mailing of notice to creditors (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-21-03).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if the entire estate subject to succession, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 and no personal representative is pending or appointed (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-23-01). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit collection up to $100,000 (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-23-01) and summary administration for estates not exceeding allowances and expenses (N.D.C.C. ch. 30.1-23).

filingFee.text: The clerk of district court charges $160 for filing a civil case for decision (N.D.C.C. § 27-05.2-03(1)(a)); a probate-specific fee was not identified in the text read.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (N.D.C.C. § 30.1-18-19).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of persons employed by the personal representative, including attorneys (N.D.C.C. ch. 30.1-18, UPC § 3-721 equivalent).

creditorClaims.text: All claims must be presented within 6 months after the death of the decedent, whether or not an executor or administrator is appointed; late claims are forever barred, except as provided in R.C. 2117.061 (R.C. 2117.06(B),(C)).

earliestClose.text: Every executor or administrator must render a final and distributive account within 6 months after appointment unless an exception applies (e.g. Ohio estate tax return, will contest, spousal election) (R.C. 2109.301(B)); the 6-month-from-death claims bar (R.C. 2117.06) is the practical earliest date.

smallEstate.text: Release from administration by court order when the estate assets are $35,000 or less, or $100,000 or less when the surviving spouse takes the whole estate under the will or by intestacy (R.C. 2113.03(A)); Ohio has no out-of-court small-estate affidavit. Not indexed.

simplified.text: Release from administration for estates up to $35,000, or up to $100,000 where the surviving spouse inherits everything (R.C. 2113.03); summary release from administration where the assets do not exceed funeral and burial expenses (R.C. 2113.031, not read).

filingFee.text: Ohio has no single statewide probate filing fee: R.C. 2101.16 (effective October 3, 2023) lists itemized probate court fees per filing (e.g. $12.00 per account), and courts may add local costs; the Franklin County Probate Court deposit schedule could not be read.

personalRepFee.text: Executors and administrators receive 4% of the first $100,000, 3% from $100,000 to $400,000 and 2% above $400,000 of personal property (including income) received and accounted for and proceeds of real property sold, plus 1% of real property not sold and 1% of non-probate property that would have been includable for Ohio estate tax as of December 31, 2012 (except joint and survivorship property) (R.C. 2113.35); extraordinary services may be allowed (R.C. 2113.36).

attorneyFee.text: Reasonable attorney fees paid by the executor or administrator are allowed as expenses of administration; the court may fix them at any time (R.C. 2113.36).

creditorClaims.text: Within 2 months after letters, the personal representative files a notice to creditors with a presentment date at least 2 months after filing, published twice and mailed to known creditors (58 O.S. § 331); contract claims not presented by that date are barred forever, with a narrow exception for out-of-state creditors who were not mailed notice (58 O.S. § 333).

earliestClose.text: No fixed minimum read beyond the 2-month presentment period of 58 O.S. § 331; distribution is ordered on final settlement of accounts (58 O.S. § 631). In estates up to $150,000 regular proceedings can be dispensed with (58 O.S. § 241).

smallEstate.text: Ten days after death, successors may collect property by affidavit if the fair market value of the decedent's Oklahoma property passing by will or intestacy, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $50,000, no personal representative is pending or appointed, and taxes and debts are paid or barred (58 O.S. § 393). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Summary administration for estates of $200,000 or less, decedents dead more than 5 years, or non-residents (58 O.S. § 245); dispensing with regular proceedings for estates up to $150,000 (58 O.S. § 241).

filingFee.text: Probate filing fees were not read.

personalRepFee.text: Absent a will provision, commissions on the whole estate accounted for: 5% of the first $1,000, 4% of the next $5,000, 2.5% above $6,000; extraordinary-service allowances may not exceed the commission amount (58 O.S. § 527).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney schedule was read; attorney fees are allowed by the district court as reasonable.

creditorClaims.text: A claim is barred from payment unless presented within its limitation period and before the later of 4 months after publication of notice to interested persons or, for creditors entitled to mailed notice, 45 days after that notice; late claims may still be paid before the final account in limited cases (ORS 115.005(2),(3)).

earliestClose.text: Not verified: the final account (ORS 116.083) follows the 4-month claims period of ORS 115.005; the court then enters a general judgment closing the estate (ORS 116.093).

smallEstate.text: Simple estate affidavit filed with the probate court when not more than $75,000 of the estate is personal property (other than manufactured homes) and not more than $200,000 is real property and manufactured homes (ORS 114.510(1)(a), 114.515); claims may be presented to the affiant within 4 months after filing. Not indexed.

simplified.text: Simple estate affidavit for estates within the $75,000 personal / $200,000 real property limits, real property included (ORS 114.505 to 114.560).

filingFee.text: Fee for a petition to appoint a personal representative: $278 if the estate is under $50,000; $591 from $50,000 to under $1 million; $882 from $1 million to under $10 million; $1,176 at $10 million or more; accounting fees $35 to $1,176 by the same bands (ORS 21.170).

personalRepFee.text: Commission on the whole estate: 7% of the first $1,000, 4% from $1,000 to $10,000, 3% from $10,000 to $50,000 and 2% above $50,000 of property subject to the court's jurisdiction (including income and gains), plus 1% of non-probate property (excluding life insurance) reportable for estate tax; further just and reasonable compensation for extraordinary services (ORS 116.173).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney schedule in the sections read; attorney fees are allowed by the court as reasonable (ORS 116.183, not read).

creditorClaims.text: Pennsylvania has no short non-claim bar date: death does not stop limitation periods, but a claim that would expire within 1 year after death is extended to 1 year after death (20 Pa.C.S. § 3383); written notice of a claim to the personal representative tolls limitations (§ 3384); claims become unenforceable after 1 year from death against bona fide purchasers of the decedent's real estate in the cases of § 3385. The one-year protection for distribution after advertisement of letters (§ 3532) could not be read.

earliestClose.text: Not verified: the rule protecting a personal representative who distributes more than 1 year after first advertisement of letters (20 Pa.C.S. § 3532) could not be read from an official source.

smallEstate.text: Settlement of small estates on petition to the orphans' court division when the decedent's property (excluding real estate and payments under § 3101, including the family exemption) has a gross value not exceeding $50,000 (20 Pa.C.S. § 3102, as amended by Act 35 of July 2, 2013, effective 60 days later, for decedents dying on or after that date). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Small estate petition for estates up to $50,000 (20 Pa.C.S. § 3102); payments to family and funeral directors of certain wages, deposits and benefits without administration (20 Pa.C.S. § 3101).

filingFee.text: Philadelphia Register of Wills probate fees depend on estate value (base fee + 20% tax + $176.25 filing fees, schedule effective September 26, 2022, published 11/18/2024): total $190.25 for $0-$250; $386.25 for $10,000.01-$50,000; $491.25 for $50,000.01-$200,000; $596.25 for $200,000.01-$300,000; rising by $105 per $100,000 bracket to $1,331.25 for the first $1,000,000; plus $75 base ($15 tax) per additional $100,000 and $750 base ($150 tax) per additional $1,000,000.

personalRepFee.text: No statutory percentage schedule in Title 20; personal representative compensation is allowed by the orphans' court as reasonable (20 Pa.C.S. § 3537, not read).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; attorney fees are allowed by the orphans' court as reasonable (20 Pa.C.S. § 3537, not read).

creditorClaims.text: Claims must be presented (filed with the probate court clerk and copied to the personal representative) within 6 months from the first publication or be forever barred, subject to leave for late claims before distribution for accident, mistake, excusable neglect or lack of adequate notice (R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 33-11-4, 33-11-5).

earliestClose.text: Not verified: distribution follows the 6-month claims period of R.I. Gen. Laws § 33-11-5.

smallEstate.text: Voluntary informal administration by verified statement filed with the probate court, 30 days after death, when the estate consists entirely of personal property worth no more than $15,000 excluding tangible personal property (R.I. Gen. Laws § 33-24-1). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Voluntary informal administration of small estates up to $15,000 of personal property (R.I. Gen. Laws § 33-24-1).

filingFee.text: Rhode Island probate courts are municipal; the Providence probate fee schedule was not read.

personalRepFee.text: Not verified: no statutory percentage schedule was read for Rhode Island executors.

attorneyFee.text: Not verified: no statutory attorney schedule was read.

creditorClaims.text: The personal representative publishes notice for 3 weeks requiring claims within 8 months after first publication (S.C. Code § 62-3-801(a)); pre-death claims are barred at the earlier of 1 year after death or the notice periods (S.C. Code § 62-3-803(a)).

earliestClose.text: The final accounting and closing filings are due after claim-contest periods and pending claim proceedings end (and 90 days after any estate tax closing letter) (S.C. Code § 62-3-1001(a)); in practice after the 8-month claims period of § 62-3-801.

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if the entire probate estate (property passing by will or intestacy), less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $45,000 (S.C. simplified.text: Summary administration when the probate estate does not exceed $45,000 plus exempt property, administration costs, funeral and last-illness expenses (S.C. Code § 62-3-1203); affidavit collection (§ 62-3-1201).

filingFee.text: Probate Court fee on the gross probate estate in the inventory: $25 under $5,000; $45 under $20,000; $67.50 under $60,000; $95 under $100,000; $95 plus 0.15% of value between $100,000 and $600,000; that amount plus 0.25% above $600,000; the same scale applies to a small estate affidavit (S.C. Code § 8-21-770(B),(C)(12)). The amount is value-based and is computed from the court-fee schedule in fees/south-carolina.json (filingFee.amount left null to avoid double counting).

personalRepFee.text: Unless the court approves more for extraordinary services, not more than 5% of the appraised value of probate personal property plus proceeds of authorized real property sales, minimum $50, plus up to 5% of estate income (S.C. Code § 62-3-719).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney schedule; the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of any attorney employed by the personal representative (S.C. Code § 62-3-721).

creditorClaims.text: The published notice gives creditors 4 months after first publication; known creditors must be notified and have the later of 4 months after appointment or 60 days after the written notice (SDCL 29A-3-801); all pre-death claims are barred 3 years after death (SDCL 29A-3-803).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 4 months after original appointment of a general personal representative (SDCL 29A-3-1003).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if the entire estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000, no personal representative is pending or appointed, and the decedent owes no Medicaid institutional-care debt to the Department of Social Services (SDCL 29A-3-1201). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit collection up to $100,000 (SDCL 29A-3-1201); summary administration proceedings ($25 clerk fee, SDCL 16-2-29(3)(i)); closing by sworn statement 4 months after appointment (SDCL 29A-3-1003).

filingFee.text: Clerk of courts fee of $75 for the probate of an estate; $25 for summary or special administration proceedings (SDCL 16-2-29).

personalRepFee.text: Personal representatives are entitled to reasonable compensation determined from seven listed factors, including time, difficulty, customary local fees and the nature and value of the assets (SDCL 29A-3-719(a)).

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys, accountants and other agents of the personal representative are entitled to reasonable compensation under the same factors (SDCL 29A-3-719(a)); reviewable by the court (SDCL 29A-3-721).

creditorClaims.text: No general bar date: a claim may be presented at any time before the estate is closed unless barred by the general statutes of limitation (Tex. Est. Code § 355.001). The personal representative must publish notice to creditors within one month after letters (§ 308.051) and may send an unsecured creditor a notice; that creditor's claim is barred if not presented before the 121st day after receipt (§§ 308.054, 355.060).

earliestClose.text: The Estates Code sets no minimum waiting period before closing; claims can be presented until the estate is closed (Tex. Est. Code § 355.001), so representatives commonly wait for the 120-day permissive-notice bar (§ 355.060).

smallEstate.text: Intestate distributees may collect the estate by a small estate affidavit approved by the judge if 30 days have passed since death, no administration is pending, and the estate assets, excluding homestead and exempt property, do not exceed $75,000 (Tex. Est. Code § 205.001, as amended effective September 1, 2017). The amount is not indexed; the affidavit is for intestate estates only.

simplified.text: A will may be probated as a muniment of title, without administration, if the estate owes no unpaid debt other than debt secured by real estate liens or administration is otherwise unnecessary (Tex. Est. Code § 257.001); a testator may also provide for independent administration free of court supervision (Tex. Est. Code § 401.001).

filingFee.text: Harris County Clerk (probate courts): associated court filing fee of $360.00 for a new estate (probate of a will, administration, heirship, muniment, small estate).

personalRepFee.text: Executors and administrators who manage the estate properly receive a 5% commission on amounts actually received or paid out in cash, capped in aggregate at 5% of the gross fair market value of the estate; no commission on cash on hand or in financial accounts at death, life insurance proceeds, or payments to heirs or legatees (Tex. Est. Code § 352.002). The court may allow reasonable compensation instead if the commission is unreasonably low or a business is managed (§ 352.003).

attorneyFee.text: The personal representative is entitled to reasonable attorney's fees necessarily incurred in connection with the proceedings and management of the estate, on proof satisfactory to the court (Tex. Est. Code § 352.051).

creditorClaims.text: A published notice requires claims within 3 months after first publication; creditors given written notice have the later of 90 days from publication or 60 days from mailing (Utah Code § 75-3-801); pre-death claims are barred at the earlier of 1 year after death or those notice periods (Utah Code § 75-3-803, effective May 7, 2025).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 4 months after original appointment of a general personal representative, after the claims period has expired (Utah Code § 75-3-1003).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if the entire estate subject to administration, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 and no personal representative is pending or appointed (Utah Code § 75-3-1201, version effective May 7, 2025); vehicles and water shares have separate rules. Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit collection up to $100,000 (Utah Code § 75-3-1201); informal probate and closing by sworn statement 4 months after appointment (§ 75-3-1003).

filingFee.text: $375 for filing any civil complaint or petition invoking the jurisdiction of a court of record not governed by another subsection (Utah Code § 78A-2-301(1)(a), version effective May 6, 2026, superseded January 1, 2027); a separate fee for filing an estate accounting runs from $15 (estate up to $50,000) to $175 (over $168,000) (§ 78A-2-301(1)(r)).

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation; if a petition seeks approval and no interested person objects, the compensation sought is deemed reasonable; on objection the court decides based on the quality, quantity and value of services (Utah Code § 75-3-718).

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys are entitled to reasonable compensation, determined by the court if an interested person objects (Utah Code § 75-3-718); reviewable under § 75-3-720.

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 4 months after first publication of notice to creditors under the Rules of Probate Procedure, or within 1 year after death if no notice was published or given (14 V.S.A. § 1203(a)).

earliestClose.text: No specific minimum period read; distribution follows the 4-month claims period (14 V.S.A. § 1203); small estate letters are effective for 1 year (14 V.S.A. § 1902(c)).

smallEstate.text: Small estate proceeding (court petition with inventory, affidavit of debts and bond without surety) when the estate has a fair market value of not more than $45,000 and consists entirely of personal property (a time-share may be included) (14 V.S.A. § 1901); objections within 14 days, otherwise approved without hearing. Vermont has no out-of-court affidavit. Not indexed.

simplified.text: Small estate proceeding for personal-property estates up to $45,000 (14 V.S.A. §§ 1901-1902); waiver of administration (14 V.S.A. ch. 80, not read).

filingFee.text: Probate filing fees are set by 32 V.S.A. § 1434 (Probate cases); the section text could not be extracted from the official page.

personalRepFee.text: An executor or administrator is allowed necessary expenses and reasonable fees for services, unless the will provides other compensation (14 V.S.A. § 1065).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; attorney fees are allowed as reasonable expenses of administration by the Probate Division.

creditorClaims.text: Virginia has no short non-claim bar for creditors; debts are proven before the commissioner of accounts (Va. Code § 64.2-550), and after 6 months from qualification the court may order creditors to show cause against distribution, after which distributees may be protected (Va. Code § 64.2-556).

earliestClose.text: A show-cause order against distribution can be sought only after 6 months from the personal representative's qualification (Va. Code § 64.2-556(A)).

smallEstate.text: Small asset affidavit by all known successors at least 60 days after death when the decedent's entire personal probate estate does not exceed $75,000, no personal representative application is pending or granted, and any will was probated (Va. Code § 64.2-601, as shown on 10/8/2026). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Virginia Small Estate Act: affidavit transfers of small assets (Va. Code § 64.2-601) and other transfers without qualification (Va. Code ch. 6).

filingFee.text: Clerk's fee for qualifying a personal representative: no fee for estates of $5,000 or less, $20 up to $50,000, $25 up to $100,000, $30 above $100,000, plus recording fees (Va. Code § 17.1-275(A)(3)); probate tax on larger estates is separate (not read).

personalRepFee.text: The commissioner of accounts allows the fiduciary reasonable expenses and reasonable compensation in the form of a commission on receipts or otherwise (Va. Code § 64.2-1208(A)); no statutory percentage.

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; attorney fees are allowed as reasonable expenses by the commissioner of accounts (Va. Code § 64.2-1208).

creditorClaims.text: If notice is published, claims are barred unless presented within 4 months after first publication (or, for creditors given actual notice, the later of 30 days after notice or 4 months after publication); reasonably ascertainable creditors not given actual notice, and all creditors if no notice was given, have 24 months after death (RCW 11.40.051).

earliestClose.text: A personal representative with nonintervention powers closes the estate by filing a declaration of completion once claims are paid or disposed of and administration is complete (RCW 11.68.110); this follows the 4-month claims period of RCW 11.40.051.

smallEstate.text: Forty days after death, a successor may collect personal property by affidavit if the decedent's entire probate estate (excluding the surviving spouse's or domestic partner's community share), less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 and no personal representative application is pending (RCW 11.62.010). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit procedure up to $100,000 (RCW 11.62.010); nonintervention probate closed by declaration of completion without court approval (RCW 11.68.110).

filingFee.text: In probate proceedings the party instituting them pays $200 when filing the first document (RCW 36.18.020(2)(f)); counties may add local surcharges.

personalRepFee.text: Absent a will provision, the personal representative receives compensation the court deems just and reasonable (RCW 11.48.210).

attorneyFee.text: An attorney performing services for the estate receives compensation the court deems just and reasonable (RCW 11.48.210); fees paid must be disclosed in the declaration of completion (RCW 11.68.110).

creditorClaims.text: The fiduciary supervisor publishes a monthly notice; claims must be exhibited to the fiduciary or the fiduciary supervisor within 60 days of the first publication of the notice, otherwise they may be excluded from the estate (W. Va. Code § 44-3A-4). The period is 60 days, not a whole number of months.

earliestClose.text: Once more than 60 days have elapsed since the notice under § 44-3A-4, the estate may be closed by short form settlement with a fiduciary affidavit and beneficiary waivers (W. Va. Code § 44-3A-4a).

smallEstate.text: Estates whose appraised assets subject to administration (excluding real estate unless the will requires its administration) total $100,000 or less are not referred to a fiduciary commissioner and are settled under the fiduciary supervisor (W. Va. Code § 44-3A-5). West Virginia has no small-estate affidavit in the sections read. Not indexed.

simplified.text: Supervision by the county fiduciary supervisor without reference to a commissioner for estates of $100,000 or less (W. Va. Code § 44-3A-5) and short form settlement after 60 days (§ 44-3A-4a).

filingFee.text: County clerk probate fees were not identified in the text read.

personalRepFee.text: Commissions on personal estate subject to administration (with its income) received and accounted for and on proceeds of real estate sold: 5% of the first $100,000, 4% from $100,000 to $400,000, 3% from $400,000 to $800,000, 2% above $800,000; plus 1% of unsold real estate and of non-probate property includable for federal estate tax (not joint and survivorship property); full compensation for ordinary services, adjustable by the county commission; a will may deviate (W. Va. Code § 44-4-12a).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney schedule; a lawyer serving as personal representative may not receive professional fees in addition to the commission (W. Va. Code § 44-4-12a(e)); other attorney fees are reasonable expenses allowed by the fiduciary commissioner (W. Va. Code § 44-4-12).

creditorClaims.text: When administration is applied for, the court or probate registrar sets a claims deadline not less than 3 nor more than 4 months from the date of the order (Wis. Stat. § 859.01); claims not filed by that date are barred (Wis. Stat. § 859.02).

earliestClose.text: Not verified: informal estates close by sworn statement (Wis. Stat. § 865.16, not read) after the 3-4 month claims deadline of § 859.01.

smallEstate.text: Transfer by affidavit when the decedent's property subject to administration in Wisconsin does not exceed $50,000 in gross value, by an heir, trustee of the decedent's revocable trust, named personal representative or former guardian (Wis. Stat. § 867.03(1g)). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Summary settlement when the estate does not exceed allowances and preferred claims, or $50,000 with a surviving spouse/domestic partner or minor children (Wis. Stat. § 867.01); summary assignment up to $50,000 subject to creditors (Wis. Stat. § 867.02); informal administration (ch. 865).

filingFee.text: Probate fees are set by Wis. Stat. § 814.66 (not read).

personalRepFee.text: Subject to court approval, commissions of 2% of the inventory value of property accounted for, less mortgages or liens, plus net principal gains, or another rate agreed in writing with the decedent or majority beneficiaries, plus reasonable sums for unusual difficulty or extraordinary services (Wis. Stat. § 857.05(2)).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney schedule; a personal representative who also serves as estate attorney receives either executor commissions or attorney fees as the court allows (Wis. Stat. § 857.05(3)).

creditorClaims.text: Claims must be filed with the clerk within the time in the notice to creditors; a claimant mailed a notice must file within 3 months after first publication or 30 days after mailing, whichever is later, or the claim is barred forever (W.S. 2-7-703(a)).

earliestClose.text: The estate closes by final decree of distribution after court approval of the final report and accounting (W.S. 2-7-813), which follows the 3-month claims period of W.S. 2-7-703; no other minimum period is stated.

smallEstate.text: Not earlier than 30 days after death, distributees may collect personal property by affidavit (filed with the clerk) if the entire Wyoming estate subject to administration, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $400,000 and no personal representative application is pending (W.S. 2-1-201(a)). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Decree of summary distribution of personal or real property (including minerals) on application filed at least 30 days after death when the entire estate, less liens, does not exceed $400,000, with 2 weeks' published notice (W.S. 2-1-205).

filingFee.text: The district court clerk charges an original filing fee of $160.00 for civil matters (W.S. 5-3-206(a)(i)); whether and how this applies to probate petitions was not confirmed.

personalRepFee.text: Fees for ordinary services computed on the probate estate accounted for: 10% of the first $1,000, 5% from $1,000 to $5,000, 3% from $5,000 to $20,000, 2% above $20,000; the court may allow more for unusual circumstances and extraordinary services (W.S. 2-7-803).

attorneyFee.text: Attorney for the estate: same schedule as the personal representative (10% / 5% / 3% / 2%) on the probate estate accounted for, plus extraordinary services; lower fees may be negotiated (W.S. 2-7-804).
